success_patterns: Several clues (Tick-Licker, the 1942 group with a 1949 chairman, the mistletoe powers clue, the Malta falcon rent) reappear almost word for word in many passages or in a Jeopardy archive. The agent filled the blank slot with the entity those passages repeat. This is already covered by Rule 3.

The 'this <noun>' pointer was answered with an instance of that noun, never an anchor named in the clue (Zimbabwe for 'this country', Salt Lake City for 'this Utah city', Appaloosa for 'this spotted breed'). This is already covered by Rule 2.

Answers were short bare entities with no descriptors, extra modifiers or sentences (Daniel Boone, mistletoe, vanilla, Falcon, Joint Chiefs of Staff). Dropped articles still matched. This is already covered by Rule 4.

The clue's own details (rare terms, dates, places) were used as anchors to choose among the passages' candidates. Every trajectory finished in one step with no second-guessing. This is already covered by Rule 3 and the 'do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity' guidance.

patch.reasoning: All eight successes came from behaviors the skill already encodes: spotting the clue near-verbatim in the passages, answering the category the 'this <noun>' pointer asks for, and giving a bare short answer. Steps 11-15 each added new narrow rules and each was rejected with a score drop, so further additions risk diluting a skill that already works on these cases. No new generalizable pattern appears in this batch, so I propose no edits.
